rv.q: A stronger lead might have helped paper over the cracks that this near-miss of a musical’s rather cheap 11th-hour twist exposes.
However, there are other problems with the writing of the show which seems thin and simplistic for three quarters of the running time.
When all is said and sung, Blaemire (Glory Days, Space Dogs), who wrote the book, music, and lyrics, has created a mixed bag of a musical.
Indeed, this confection got pulled out of the oven before it was ready to be seen.
I will only tell you that when Soon finally opens it, it is heartbreaking in the best possible way.
The experience of watching this show is engaging, and it’s packed full of metaphor and meaning while also maintaining a plot that is easy to follow.
The trees may be ablaze, but this is Manhattan, so groceries can still be ordered, and thus romance finds its way into Charlie’s homestead.
Soon grapples with both the existential and practical side of dying. But its perspective on living rarely resonates emotionally.

cn.t: Critics are mixed on this intimate chamber musical about climate anxiety and isolation, praising its honest premise and performances but finding its tonal shifts awkward and its execution uneven.

vr.q: I think it's such a special show
